subject: Hyperion Health SLA/SLO questionnaire — observability & credit examples

Subject: Hyperion SLO questionnaire v2 (request)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is Hyperion's updated SLA/SLO questionnaire (v2) — the procurement and platform teams want specific measurement and evidence examples for availability and latency guarantees. We're hoping to finalize answers before we start legal redlines.

Key asks:
- Confirm the precise measurement window and sampling method you would use for 99th percentile latency on the text generation endpoint.
- Provide an example monthly calculation (single-region and multi-region scenarios) showing how any service credits would be computed.
- Clarify what counts as an "availability incident" for crediting (regional outage vs. transient host errors).

Can you get back to us with a completed response and any attachments by EOD Jan 28? If you prefer, a short call with your SRE/product folks early next week works as well.

Attached: Hyperion_SLO_Questionnaire_v2.docx

Thanks,

Jenna — thanks for sending this over.

We're on it. Marissa (Solutions) will lead the answers for measurement and credits; Neha (Security & Compliance) will review the definition of incidents and evidence requirements. I'll consolidate into a single response pack and return by the 28th.

Quick note up front to set expectations:
- For latency we use a request-weighted p99 computed from production ingress traces over a rolling 1-minute sampling cadence (see attached example in our response).
- Availability incidents are primarily derived from our region-level health checks combined with synthetic probe failures; we'll include examples and edge cases (e.g., control-plane-only vs data-plane outages).

If you want a short walkthrough, Marissa can do a 20-minute call Tue morning (Jan 26) to run through the methodology.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-27T16:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Hyperion SLO questionnaire v2 (request) — draft responses attached

Jenna — attaching our response workbook (Redwood_Hyperion_SLO_Response.xlsx) and a short sample observability report (monthly-observability-sample.pdf). Below are the high-level answers and the worked example for credits. The workbook contains cell-level formulas and a sample telemetry snapshot.

1) Latency measurement (text-generate endpoint)
- Metric: request_latency_ms (end-to-end, client-facing).
- Aggregation window: 1-minute buckets collected at ingestion, retained for 90 days for SLO verification.
- Method: request-weighted percentile calculation over the window; p99 reported as the 99th percentile of aggregated latency across successful requests in the measurement window.
- Sampling: continuous telemetry; if traffic < 1 req/sec in a minute bucket we mark the bucket as "insufficient" and exclude from percentile calculation for that minute. We show the numerator/denominator in the workbook.

2) Availability definition
- Region-level availability = percentage of successful requests routed to healthy data-plane endpoints when the customer's traffic region is selected.
- Incident trigger: region-level synthetic probe failure sustained for >= 5 consecutive minutes AND confirmed reduction in successful request routing (>0.5% error delta vs baseline) for the same window.
- Exclusions: customer-side network blackholes, specified maintenance windows, and misconfiguration of customer routing. We'll provide tooling hooks to correlate provider-side telemetry with customer HTTP status codes to support disputes.

3) Service credits — worked example (single-region monthly)
- Monthly window size: calendar month.
- SLO: 99.95% region availability target.
- Example: If observed availability = 99.60% in Jan, shortfall = 0.35 percentage points. Our credit matrix (included in the workbook) maps shortfall bands to credits (e.g., 0.25–0.5 -> 10% monthly credit). The spreadsheet shows the calculation and prorated credits when multiple incidents contribute to the shortfall.
- Multi-region: we measure each region independently and apply credits for the customer region(s) configured in the routing policy; if customer uses active-active across regions, credits are proportional to request weight per affected region (examples provided).

4) Measurement evidence package
- We will provide a monthly SLO report containing: aggregated p99 latency, request counts, synthetic probe history (per-region), incident timelines with root-cause tags, and the raw sampling buckets used for percentile computation (CSV). We include examples in the sample PDF.

5) Timing and dispute resolution
- Measurement completed within 5 business days after month end; disputes to be raised within 30 days with joint evidence exchange and a 14-day resolution SLA.

Attachments: Redwood_Hyperion_SLO_Response.xlsx (workbook with formulas), monthly-observability-sample.pdf (example report)

Let me know if you want any of the workbook sheets expanded into a walk-through — happy to join a short call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@hyperionhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Hyperion SLO questionnaire v2 (request) — draft responses attached

Marissa / Karthik — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for. A couple of follow-ups from the procurement and platform teams after reviewing the workbook:

1) "Regional outage" definition — can you explicitly call out whether a control-plane-only degradation (no data-plane API errors, but slower provisioning and control-plane API failures) would ever count toward region availability? We saw references to control-plane vs data-plane in the workbook but want a single-sentence decision for the contract.

2) Monthly report format — is the CSV you mentioned compatible with automated ingestion into our internal incident system (we can share a sample schema)? If not, would you provide a one-time mapping guide?

3) For the credit example, can you add one worked example that shows two separate incidents in the same month and how credits are prorated? The workbook shows the bands but the legal team wants an explicit two-incident calculation.

If you can send a short updated sheet addressing 1–3 by Feb 2 we'll move this into Legal for redlines. Also, please include a single-page summary (one PDF) that we can attach to the SOW.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Jenna
Senior Procurement Manager
Hyperion Health
jenna.liu@hyperionhealth.com
